I tried the finished app directly, and it does everything we settled on. I saved a page and it stuck around when I looked again, so my collection genuinely persists. Saving the same page a second time didn't make a duplicate — and it even recognized the same page when I added newsletter tracking bits and a jump-to-section to the address, which is that nice touch I'd hoped for. Search found my page regardless of capital letters, read-later could be turned on and off, a page saved cleanly with a sensible fallback when its details couldn't be fetched, and deleting cleared it back to a tidy empty collection. Editing, tags, and the confirm-before-delete safety are all there too.

(One small note for your records: the static files copied into this round's folder are actually the earlier click-through prototype rather than the finished app — but the real app at the live address is the genuine, working build, and that's what I judged.)

This is exactly the organized, low-effort bookmark home I set out wanting. I accept it as the completed first cycle. Thank you for the careful work.
